messages:
maria: Heads-up — support just escalated multiple customers seeing p95 latency spike on /v1/generate since ~11:02 UTC. Affected region: eu-west-1. Visible in traces as long tail on server-side token gen. link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/p95-spike
oncall-bot: ALERT: p95_latency /v1/generate > 800ms (eu-west-1) — started 11:02:14 UTC — alert_id=ALRT-9182
samir: pinging runtime — any infra changes?
lee: nothing deployed in eu-west-1 during window. Seeing increased queue length on g4x pools and a dozen 503s from one host (gpu-32-07). Logs show repeated kernel timeouts on step 3 for long-context requests.
maria: customer examples attached in support ticket #5782 — mostly chat sessions with >2k token prompts, some large system messages.
jordan: are these customers on hosted or dedicated?
zane: 2 hosted, 1 dedicated (reserved pool). Dedicated pool doesn't show CPU pressure but GPU utilization is spiky with high tail.
samir: short checklist: 1) apply temporary tighter rate-limit on /v1/generate for eu-west-1 2) enable model fallback to smaller variant 3) enable circuit-breaker to fail fast for new sessions 4) kick autoscale on dedicated pool if possible
lee: I can push a temporary circuit-breaker policy at the edge. Proposed rule: if p95>600ms for 2m then return 503 FastFail for requests with session_age<60s and increase priority for cached prompts. Config snippet:
```
edge.policy.circuit_breaker:
  window: 120s
  p95_threshold_ms: 600
  fastfail_session_age: 60
  fallback_model: redwood-medium-quant
  action: fastfail
```

maria: support will inform affected customers of rollback/fallback. Jordan, can we auto-switch their routes to eu-central until this is resolved?
jordan: we can, but must check compliance/regional policy. For the two hosted customers it's OK; the dedicated customer requires approval. I'll ping sales for quick signoff.
zane: meanwhile, Samir — can we throttle large-context requests to bucket them into async jobs? That would reduce tail pressure.
samir: yes — add rule to limit prompt token count >1200 to async queue with a 30s client notice. Quick curl to flip limiter in eu-west: 
```
curl -X POST https://edge-api.redwood.internal/configs/limit -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_KEY" -d '{"scope":"eu-west-1","route":"/v1/generate","max_tokens_sync":1200}'
```

lee: I'm enabling the edge circuit-breaker now and flipping fallback routing for hosted customers to redwood-medium-quant. Leaving dedicated unchanged until Jordan confirms.
oncall-bot: ACTION: circuit-breaker enabled by lee at 11:08:42 UTC. fallback routing enabled for hosted customers.
maria: initial observations: p95 dropped from ~850ms to ~480ms within 90s. p99 still noisy but trending down.
samir: I'll schedule a short eviction of KV cache warm-up for the fallback model to absorb traffic. Also increasing batch size cap on medium-quant to improve throughput.
jordan: sales confirmed dedicated customer consent for eu-central fallback (approved). I'll coordinate the route switch — target 11:20 UTC.
lee: route switch done for dedicated customer at 11:21 — verified traces now show requests hitting eu-central and p95 for that customer back to ~420ms.
maria: support updated ticket #5782 and notified SLAs. Customers acknowledged and will continue monitoring.
zane: follow-ups: - add auto-fallback policy to runbook (if p95>600ms for 2m, route hosted to fallback model/region) - add a throttle for >1200 token sync requests - add a dedicated autoscale pre-warm for spikes - postmortem to identify kernel timeouts on g4x host
samir: adding short-term metric watch: set an alert to notify if p99>1500ms for 5m. Also adding an incident tag so we can track changes.
maria: good work team. Can someone own the postmortem doc? Samir or Lee?
samir: I can draft the postmortem and include kernel logs and host replacement notes.
lee: I'll lead remediation on runtime kernel timeouts and coordinate patching with infra.
jordan: I'll update the SLO guardrails doc with the new auto-fallback rules and get legal/ops signoff for cross-region fallbacks.
maria: closing thread for now — reopen if p95 trends back up. :thumbsup:
